idiom_name: pure arrow functions, spread copies and non-mutating array methods; Object.freeze for shallow runtime protection
implementation_notes: JavaScript offers no enforcement to lean on: const creates an immutable binding, not an immutable value, and Object.freeze is shallow, so nested objects stay mutable (in non-strict mode a write to a frozen property even fails silently). The realization is therefore a convention: queries take values and return new objects built with spread, and state changes live in explicitly named command functions. The non-mutating array methods (map, filter, reduce, concat, slice, and ES2023's toSorted/toReversed/toSpliced) are the query vocabulary, while push, splice, sort, reverse and direct assignment are the command vocabulary. Freeze module-level constants and returned configuration so accidental writes fail loudly at runtime.
pitfalls: Array.prototype.sort and reverse mutate the receiver and return it; use toSorted/toReversed (ES2023) or copy first.
Object.freeze is shallow and sloppy-mode writes fail silently, so a nested object can still be changed and the mistake surfaces much later.
Date.now, Math.random, locale-dependent Intl formatting and module-level mutable state are hidden inputs; pass them in as parameters.
